To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inclusion of aligned spin effects in the gravitational wave search template bank improves the sensitivity of the search pipeline to gravitational waves from binary black hole systems with 0≤ χ ≤ 0.85, and that the use of aligned spin templates in the search improves the estimation of binary mass and spin parameters.

we have developed an analysis pipeline with increased sensitivity to binary black hole gravitational waves with aligned spins, and that this analysis pipeline can be used to detect gravitational waves from binary black holes with aligned spins with a signal-to-noise ratio of at least 8, and to accurately estimate the masses and spins of these binary black holes.

the inclusion of spin information in the template bank improves the sensitivity of the search pipeline to binary black hole signals, that the inclusion of spins in the templates improves the accuracy of the parameter recovery, and that the inclusion of spinning templates in a search pipeline is a promising direction to improve the sensitivity of searches for gravitational waves from colescing binary black hole systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of gravitational waves from binary black holes with spin.
the detection of gravitational wave signals emitted by binary black holes with aligned spins and the measurement of the binary’s parameters.
the development of a search pipeline that improves sensitivity to gravitational waves emitted from coalescing aligned-spin binary black hole systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we demonstrate for the first times a search pipeline with increased sensitivity to gravitational waves signals from coalescing binaries with aligned spins.

we have developed and demonstrated a search pipeline with increased sensitivity to coalescing binary systems with nonprecessional spins aligned with the orbital angular momentum, and we have measured the increase in observable volume and accuracy in parameter estimation for such signals.
the inclusion of spin in the search templates has a significant effect on the search sensitivity and recovery of binary black hole systems with nonprecessed spins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to detect binary black holes with a spin aligned to the orbital plane with a sensitivity improvement of up to 50%.
we have demonstrated the use of a phenomenological waveform family to construct template banks for use in a search pipeline.
we have shown the feasibility of a pipeline that can detect and characterize gravitational wave signals from spinning binary black holes with high sensitivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the search for binary black holes with aligned spins can benefit from a modest template bank extension to χ∼0.85.
the inclusion of spinning template families in searches for gravitational waves from binary black holes can significantly improve the sensitivity to the signals.
a pipeline using aligned-spin templates can detect more binary black hole signals and recover them with more accurate mass estimates than a pipeline using nonspinning templates.
